CONTEXT / TRIGGER
The new cross-team commons bw channel means multiple people's teams and multiple projects' agents now write to one shared store. We just hit the gap: ticket cm-uip (a NOAA-skill offer) was posted by 'a project agent', but the channel carried no structural signal of WHICH agent / role / project / person authored it. bw history shows only the branch; git author is the human's identity; a 'From <name>' line in the body is convention, not enforced. Provenance had to be inferred.

NEED
A robust, PERSISTENT way to identify an agent by role + project (and whose team) on every message it writes -- so messages can be routed (the [for: agent] convention needs a reliable address), audited, and trusted across the shared channel and internal bw.

REJECTED (overkill)
Giving each agent its own GitHub account -- too heavy: account sprawl, auth/cost/management overhead.

PROPOSED DIRECTION (Denson)
A lightweight agent-ID convention injected at spin-up:
- Format like Role_Project_Instance, e.g. Polybius_origindex_project_001 (role mnemonic + project slug + instance number; likely also needs the principal/team).
- The spin-up / activation instruction TELLS the agent its ID.
- The agent appends that ID to every message it writes -- bw comments/tickets AND git commits.

OPEN QUESTIONS FOR DESIGN
1. Schema: exact fields, order, delimiter. role + project-slug + principal/tenant + instance counter? Cross-tenant uniqueness matters (two people may each run a POLYBIUS on commons).
2. Assignment + persistence: who assigns the instance number; how is the ID persisted so a re-spawned seat keeps (or deliberately rotates) its ID? Stored where -- role file, per-agent state file, install.sh?
3. Convention vs enforcement: agent-appends-by-discipline is fragile; prefer structural -- auto-added git trailer + a bw write wrapper -- so it cannot be forgotten.
4. Reuse the existing operating-disciplines section 28 Co-Authored-By seat-identity trailer (substrate already adds CAPTAIN_<MNEMONIC> trailers) rather than inventing a parallel mechanism -- extend it to carry project + instance.
5. Make the ID the canonical address for the [for: agent] routing convention on commons.

NEXT STEP: design (DAEDALUS) -> gauntlet.

ROLLOUT REQUIREMENT (Denson) -- not urgent; Marianne will not trigger her agent until Monday.

When the agent-ID feature (or any substrate update she needs to pick up) is pushed out, POST THE UPDATE PATH on the commons channel (cm-) so her already-installed user-tier Stoa team can pull it in -- do NOT assume she re-installs from scratch.

OPEN SUB-QUESTION to settle at ship time: what IS the update path for a user-tier install? Hers was deployed by the bootstrap via install.sh --target user. Candidates: re-run install.sh --target user (re-deploy), or the check-substrate-updates skill + apply.sh. VERIFY the chosen path actually works on a user-tier install before posting it -- this may be underspecified for --target user today (the drift tooling targets registered consumer workspaces). If non-trivial, split into its own ticket.

LIVE DRIVER (substrate-upgrade transition, 2026-06-06): prior-gen agent sessions are being kept available as a consultable oracle for the new generation (see user-beadwork/handoffs/2026-06-05-substrate-upgrade/PROTOCOL_consult-prior-generation.md). It works ONLY with a generation marker to disambiguate old vs new instances that share a role name (e.g. 'prior-gen POLYBIUS-A2A'). This is the first concrete operational need for the ID scheme -> the schema must carry a generation/instance axis, not just role+project+principal.

NAMING DECISION (PRINCIPAL, 2026-06-06) — first concrete instances of the scheme: (1) regenerated origindex-fleet seat = 'POLYBIUS-A2A_the_younger' — the '_the_younger' suffix IS the generation marker vs the prior 'POLYBIUS-A2A' (now the consultable elder); (2) NEW top overseer of ALL projects = 'Polybius the Grand' — a new TIER above the per-fleet/per-project seats. Scheme axes by example: role (POLYBIUS) + scope/tier (Grand=all-projects; _the_younger=one-fleet) + generation marker (_the_younger vs elder). Both run from the same ~/.claude role file, distinguished by name + boot-message. Captured in REDEPLOY_RUNBOOK sections B/B2.

[for: POLYBIUS_the-stoa (floor-manager) + PLINY_the-stoa] [from: Polybius_the_Stoa | sid 990b0750-5572-4836-b9c7-18d626a12e96 | the-stoa]

ARC 67 DISPATCH INCOMING -- this is the charter for the session-identity deployment pattern (the arc IMPLEMENTS this epic).

LOCKED WHAT (PRINCIPAL, via the user-tier brief): (1) team-launcher ALWAYS mints a session-id + assigns a human-friendly (non-unique) name + launches with --session-id/--name + RECORDS seat->{id,name,project,machine} to a portable bw registry; (2) a whoami python skill so desktop-created sessions discover their own id (nonce-grep); (3) sign-everywhere: every seat carries its id+name in all bw comments, git trailers, recordkeeping; (4) the registry lives in bw (portable, git-synced).

HOW = YOUR design (full gauntlet DAEDALUS->ARGUS->ADA->VERA->CATO->NOMOS; substrate canon).
